title: This Wasp Doesn't Kill a Tarantula. What It Does Is Worse
subject: tarantula hawk wasp

scenes.text: This wasp doesn't kill a tarantula. It does something worse.
The tarantula hawk stings it between the legs. The venom paralyzes the spider but keeps it alive.
Then the wasp drags the helpless tarantula into a burrow and lays one egg on its belly.
The egg hatches. The larva bores in and feeds, sparing the vital organs so the spider stays alive as long as possible.
A sting from the adult wasp scores four out of four on the Schmidt pain scale, second only to the bullet ant.
The pain lasts about five minutes. For the tarantula, it lasts weeks.

description:
The tarantula hawk wasp doesn't kill a tarantula.
It paralyzes it, drags it into a burrow, and lays an egg on it, and the larva eats the living spider.
Would you rather take that sting or the bullet ant's?
thumbnail_text: THE WASP THAT KEEPS ITS PREY ALIVE
first_comment: Researcher Justin Schmidt called the sting blinding, fierce and shockingly electric. Would you ever test it?
